content.text:
**No, Borobudur is not one of the (New) Seven Wonders of the World in any official or primary sense.** It was never a winner of the 2007 New7Wonders campaign, nor a finalist among the 21 shortlisted candidates. It is, however, a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 1991 under the official name "Borobudur Temple Compounds"). It appears in many informal/popular lists due to its architectural grandeur and cultural significance in Indonesia, but it was never part of the ancient Seven Wonders of the World.[[1]](https://world.new7wonders.com/lisbon-on-07-07-2007/)[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/)

Here is a precise breakdown with sources (primarily official sites like new7wonders.com, whc.unesco.org, and reliable references like Wikipedia summaries of primary info or Britannica-adjacent knowledge; claims are labeled **VERIFIED** for direct primary/official sources or **REPORTED** for secondary/popular mentions).

### 1. New7Wonders of the World (2007, New7Wonders Foundation)
- **Borobudur was never a winner.** The official winners (announced July 7, 2007, in Lisbon) are: Great Wall of China, Petra (Jordan), Chichén Itzá (Mexico), Christ the Redeemer (Brazil), Colosseum (Italy), Machu Picchu (Peru), and Taj Mahal (India). The Giza Pyramids received honorary status as the sole survivor of the ancient list.[[1]](https://world.new7wonders.com/lisbon-on-07-07-2007/)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_7_Wonders_of_the_World)
  - **VERIFIED** (primary/official): new7wonders.com/wonders/ (lists winners and the 21 finalists explicitly; no Borobudur) and contemporaneous reports of the Lisbon declaration.[[4]](https://world.new7wonders.com/wonders/)
- **Borobudur was not a finalist.** The 21 official finalists (from which the 7 were chosen via global voting) included sites like Stonehenge, Hagia Sophia, Alhambra, Acropolis of Athens, Angkor Wat, Statue of Liberty, Moai, Giza Pyramids, Kremlin, Eiffel Tower, Sydney Opera House, Timbuktu, and others—but **not Borobudur**.[[4]](https://world.new7wonders.com/wonders/)[[4]](https://world.new7wonders.com/wonders/)
  - **VERIFIED** (primary/official): new7wonders.com (full 21 finalists list).
- Some secondary sources (e.g., regional articles) describe it as "nominated," a "candidate," or having reached a "final round" informally, but this is not supported by the official shortlist.[[5]](https://seasia.co/2025/07/13/sorry-indonesians-borobudur-was-never-one-of-the-new-7-wonders-of-the-world)
  - **REPORTED** (secondary): Various blogs, news, or social media; contradicted by the official finalist roster.

### 2. UNESCO World Heritage Site Status
- **Yes**, Borobudur **is** a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
  - **Exact inscription year**: 1991 (15th session of the World Heritage Committee).[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borobudur)
  - **Official listing name**: Borobudur Temple Compounds (ID 592; criteria i, ii, vi). It includes the main temple plus the related Mendut and Pawon temples.[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/)
  - **VERIFIED** (primary source): whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/ (official UNESCO page with inscription details, description, and 1991 decision).[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/)

### 3. Why Many Sources/Lists Call Borobudur a "Wonder of the World"
This is informal/popular usage, not tied to any official Seven Wonders list:
- Its scale (world's largest Buddhist temple), intricate reliefs, Buddhist cosmology symbolism, and engineering as an 8th–9th century monument make it a standout archaeological and cultural achievement in Southeast Asia.
- It features prominently in Indonesian tourism, education (e.g., school materials highlighting national heritage), and global "wonders of architecture" or "must-see" lists.
- Popularity boosted by its UNESCO status, restorations (including UNESCO-supported work in the 1970s–80s), and status as a major pilgrimage/tourist site.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borobudur)
  - **REPORTED** (secondary/popular): Wikipedia summaries, travel sites, Indonesian blogs/textbooks, Quora/Facebook posts, and informal "wonders" compilations. No primary official endorsement as one of the "Seven Wonders."[[7]](http://indonesia-fascination.blogspot.com/2012/10/borobudur-temple-one-of-seven-wonder-of.html)

### 4. Ancient Seven Wonders of the World
- **No**, Borobudur was never on the ancient list. That classical list (from Hellenistic Greek sources, ~2nd century BCE) includes only: Great Pyramid of Giza, Hanging Gardens of Babylon, Statue of Zeus at Olympia, Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, Colossus of Rhodes, and Lighthouse of Alexandria. All are far older (mostly pre-Common Era) and located in the Mediterranean/Middle East/North Africa region. Borobudur dates to the 8th–9th centuries CE in Java, Indonesia.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_7_Wonders_of_the_World)
  - **VERIFIED** (primary/historical consensus): Standard references (e.g., Britannica, Wikipedia citing ancient sources like Antipater of Sidon); no inclusion of Borobudur or any Southeast Asian site.

**Key source URLs demanded**:
- New7Wonders official: https://world.new7wonders.com/wonders/ (winners + 21 finalists) and https://world.new7wonders.com/ (campaign site).[[8]](https://www.new7wonders.com/)
- UNESCO official: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/ (inscription details).[[2]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/)
- Supporting: Wikipedia pages (summarizing the above primaries) and Britannica-style historical lists for the ancient wonders.

In short, Borobudur is a genuine world-class heritage site worthy of admiration, but its "wonder" status is cultural/popular rather than from the official New7Wonders or ancient lists.
